hook_text: The Sahara exists because it rains at the equator. One loop of air makes the jungle AND the desert — and your whole year hangs on it.
clip_script: The circulation topic is a courier problem: the equator was over-delivered heat and the poles were shorted, so the atmosphere runs courier routes to balance the books. Route one: air above the equator heats like the air over a fire, rises, drifts poleward at altitude, cools, and comes back down around thirty degrees — a closed loop, the first conveyor belt. Now look hard at the descending end, because it hides the trick that unlocks half the map: sinking air is dry air pressing downward — it dissolves cloud instead of building it — and thirty degrees is precisely the latitude where the planet's great deserts lie. Sahara, Kalahari margin, the Australian interior: not coincidences, but the dry exhaust of the equator's rising rain. One loop manufactures both the rainforest and the desert. And on a spinning planet, nothing travels straight. Stand on a turning merry-go-round and roll a ball to a friend: the ball runs true through space, yet from your rotating seat its path curves away. Winds ride the same illusion, curving left in the southern hemisphere — which is why the trades reach our east coast from the south-east and the winter storms strike the Cape from the south-west. Slide the whole machine with the seasons, and Johannesburg dries out in the very months Cape Town gets soaked. One migrating machine, two rain calendars, one country.
visual_style: A glowing loop of air rising over animated jungle and sinking onto sand dunes; a world map lighting up desert belts along thirty degrees; a sketched merry-go-round with a ball curving away from its thrower; a split-screen calendar of Johannesburg thunderstorms against Cape Town winter rain.
mood: Revelatory — the satisfying click of one mechanism explaining half the map.
pacing: Steady build around the loop, a snap reveal on the desert belt, playful beat on the merry-go-round, clean two-city landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and lock in the whole physical year before your final exams.
